apps.name: Accessible IPTV
apps.subtitle: IPTV player built for VoiceOver.
apps.localizedDescription:
A screen-reader-friendly IPTV player for iPhone and iPad, with CarPlay audio. Xtream Codes logins, Stalker portals, M3U URLs and M3U files; Live TV, Movies and Series with groups, favourites and search, including voice search. XMLTV guide with On now, guide search and catch-up. The libVLC player plays raw MPEG-TS, HLS, MKV and MP4, picks audio description, remembers tracks per channel, reconnects dropped streams, casts to Chromecast and keeps playing with the screen locked. Record, schedule recordings and download. 14 languages.

Every list row is one VoiceOver stop with its extra choices in the Actions rotor; real, always-visible buttons; headings everywhere.

versions.localizedDescription: Siri can now play channels it could not find before. Channels are offered to Siri by their spoken name, without provider prefixes or quality labels, with the provider label and the channel number as alternate names; unnamed entries stay distinguishable by number or group. A channel whose spoken name matches exactly is chosen outright instead of competing with similarly named channels. Needs iOS 27 or later.

Siri AI can play a channel now. Requests to watch a channel in Accessible IPTV used to answer that the app does not support playing content through Siri; the app now adopts Apple's audio playback schemas (live radio station entity and Play audio intent), so Siri plays the channel it found. Needs iOS 27 or later; iPhone and iPad on iOS 17 to 26 are unchanged. Shuffle, repeat and queue positions do not apply to a live channel and are ignored.

Siri and Apple Intelligence now get a written description of every channel, guide and search action, in all 14 languages, so requests match more reliably. More ways to ask with the app name: Watch, Play, Tune to, Put on and Start a channel, plus Watch live TV. Settings has a Siri and Shortcuts row that opens this app page in Shortcuts: Apple requires App Shortcut phrases to include the app name, and a shortcut of your own is the way to use a phrase without it.

Spotlight: search live channels by name or number from the Home screen and pick a result to start watching. Shortcuts: Find Channels filters by name, group and number, with sorting, limits and the chosen channel returned for later actions. Siri and Apple Intelligence can discover indexed channels on iOS 18 or later. Channel matching now ignores provider punctuation and supports partial names. All 14 languages updated.

Siri: Play, Tune to and Watch channels in Accessible IPTV. Clean spoken names ignore provider prefixes and quality labels. Favourites and recent channels refresh Siri vocabulary. Say Watch TV in Accessible IPTV to search any live channel when prompted. Help covers personal shortcuts for commands without the app name in all 14 languages.

Guide fixes: programme lists now load in windows with a More row, one channel guide has a filter and day headings, past programmes speak their date, loads announce their count, the Guide section has a channel picker, and guide search narrows as you type instead of rescanning.

Playback destination is now one list: This device, AirPlay device, and every Cast device labelled as a Cast device. The separate Prepare AirPlay video button is gone; picking an AirPlay device starts conversion automatically when the stream needs it. Converted video now keeps the source resolution instead of a 720p cap.

AVPlayer now handles compatible HLS, MP4 and other native media, with VLCKit fallback for unsupported formats and failures. On iPhone and iPad, Prepare AirPlay video converts other IPTV video on the device to H.264/AAC HLS (up to 720p30) for AirPlay, and the playback destination uses the same conversion for Chromecast. No separate server is required. Choose audio and subtitles before casting and keep the app open on the receiver Wi-Fi. Protected streams, unavailable encoders and device performance can prevent conversion; local playback remains available.

Native iPhone tabs and categories-first browsing. Persistent video miniplayer and native background and lock-screen playback. Siri and Shortcuts tune channels, read now and next, search the guide and control playback. SharePlay shares channel selection and playback through FaceTime using each participant’s own playlist/login; native coordination for seekable movies, episodes and catch-up. Live timing depends on provider buffers. Translated controls and help in 14 languages. SharePlay installation requires the Group Activities entitlement.

A category opens in a fraction of a second again. The list was building a row for every entry in the category instead of only the rows on screen; it is now built 2,000 rows at a time, and where there are more the end of the list has a More button saying how many are left.

Measurement build for the slow category switch: when a category change or a list load takes over a second, the status line says what it cost. Also, the guide lookup a row makes is remembered for half a minute, so redrawing or scrolling does not repeat the same query for every row.

Choosing a category is much faster on a big account: the channel list is built fresh for the category you chose instead of working out the difference from the previous one, which took seconds with tens of thousands of channels. Rows no longer animate when a whole list is replaced.

An audit of the player, the recorder, CarPlay and voice search: recording a channel twice in a minute no longer writes both to one file, casting no longer ends with a wrong error, CarPlay playback keeps its lock screen and steering wheel play and pause, and the Voice button no longer crashes when pressed twice.

An audit of 0.1.4: search finds a name whose accented letter the feed writes as a separate mark, names of the same rank sort by length again, a refreshed playlist no longer leaves a channel on an old guide entry, and deleting the last playlist clears the list.
The category list on a phone is now a lazy list that opens from one button, so a provider with hundreds of categories is no longer slow to open or to redraw.
No more long freeze when the app opens, comes back into focus, or switches between Live TV, Movies and Series: the guide index and the group counts no longer run on the main thread.
Search is much faster: a keystroke over 50,000 channels went from 0.16 s to 0.01 s. A fresh launch no longer hashes every channel on the main thread.

Much less CPU while the guide imports: the guide reader is about 12 times faster and skips channels you do not have. Xtream movie and series lists load about twice as fast. The channel list no longer redraws on every status change; fewer background timers in the player and recorder.

First iOS release, a port of Accessible IPTV Client for Android 0.2.11: Xtream, Stalker and M3U; guide with catch-up; libVLC player that plays raw MPEG-TS; recordings; 14 languages. Built for VoiceOver.
